title: Minimize Rounding Error to Meet Target
summary: Given an array of prices and a target, round each price to either floor or ceiling so that the rounded array sums to the target.
statement: Given an array of prices and a target, round each price to either floor or ceiling so that the rounded array sums to the target. Return the smallest rounding error, defined as the sum of the absolute differences between each rounded price and the original price, as a string with three decimal places. If it is impossible to achieve the target sum, return "-1".
constraints: Prices have exactly three decimal digits and are nonnegative.
Round each up or down to reach target and return minimum error with three decimals, or -1.
reference_solution:
def minimum_rounding_error(prices, target):
 values=[int(x.replace('.','')) for x in prices];floor=sum(x//1000 for x in values);need=target-floor;fractions=sorted((x%1000 for x in values if x%1000),reverse=True)
 if need<0 or need>len(fractions):return '-1'
 error=sum(1000-x for x in fractions[:need])+sum(fractions[need:]);return f'{error/1000:.3f}'

hints: Flooring everything establishes the baseline; target determines exactly how many values must round up.
Rounding fraction f up costs 1-f instead of f, so larger fractions give greater savings.
Sort fractions descending and round up the required count.
The number of upward choices is fixed, and selecting greatest savings minimizes total absolute error.
